summary: Backend-only regression of Tennis Player Auction after MongoDB -> Firebase Realtime Database migration. 30/30 pytest cases PASS (24 prior auth/authz/bidding/full-flow + 6 new Firebase-migration tests). Firebase normalization (to_list + normalize) verified across multiple consecutive finalize operations: 5 captains awarded the entire UTR 5.0 pool, pool transitioned cleanly to UTR 4.5 (pool key still present and length 5), first 4.5 bid at $10k accepted, $9k rejected. Skip correctly rotates current player to end of pool with isRetry=True and retryCount=1. Persistence verified with fresh requests.Session (no client cache) after create+bid+finalize. Reset restores initial 14-captains-only state with pools full. Initial-state checks: 14 teams pre-assigned captains with budget=100000-captain_price, pools utr_5_5 and utr_5_25 fully consumed by captains and serialized as [] (Firebase drops empty arrays but normalize() restores them), first auctioned player is from UTR 5.0 @ base $12,000. Auth/authz matrix unchanged and green (admin/captain code+PIN, wrong PIN -> 401, captain create/finalize/skip/reset -> 403, captain bid other team -> 403, admin can't bid -> 403, unique-bid, below-base, bad-increment, budget-reserve rules all enforced). No code changes were needed; all behaviour matches the pre-migration spec.
action_items: Optional carry-over (iter_1/iter_2): POST /api/auctions/{sid}/reset is not optimistic-concurrency safe (full set without version gate via fb_set). Could overwrite an in-flight transaction. Consider gating on version inside a transaction.
Optional: server.py still uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup'); switch to lifespan context manager.
Cosmetic: backend/.env still has the now-unused MONGO_URL/DB_NAME keys after the Firebase migration; safe to remove.
critical_code_review_comments: normalize()/to_list() correctly handle Firebase's array<->index-keyed-dict ambiguity and dropped-empty-array behaviour. Pool order is preserved deterministically via sorted(int(k)).

run_txn() uses RTDB transaction on the whole /auctions/{sid} node — returning `current` (unchanged) on validation errors is the correct way to reject without a write. Concurrency on bid/finalize/skip is safe.
POST /reset writes via fb_set (not a transaction) — only admin path so the race risk is low, but a concurrent bid mid-reset could be silently overwritten.
firebase_db.init() is idempotent (checks firebase_admin._apps) and is called both at import time and in @app.on_event('startup'); fine but on_event is deprecated.
Auth/authz unchanged from prior iterations: bcrypt PIN (72-byte safe slice), JWT with role+teamId, idempotent code-based seeding from seed.get_accounts().
seed_data_creation: Used auto-seeded ADMIN/731902 and TEAM1..TEAM14 captains from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Created multiple short-lived auction sessions (unique 6-char sessionIds) under /auctions/* in Firebase; no teardown performed (each session is isolated by sessionId).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend URL: https://player-bidding-8.preview.emergentagent.com (also in frontend/.env as EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL). Data layer is Firebase Realtime DB (databaseURL from FIREBASE_DB_URL env, service-account JSON in FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_B64). Tests live in /app/backend/tests/ and use HTTP only — no direct Firebase fixtures. To clean up a specific auction node: `from dotenv import load_dotenv; load_dotenv(); import firebase_db as fb; fb.init(); fb.ref(f'auctions/{sid}').delete()`. Key normalization rule: pools persist as index-keyed dicts in Firebase, normalize() converts back to ordered lists; empty arrays come back as None and normalize() replaces with []. First auctioned player is always UTR 5.0 @ $12,000 because UTR 5.5 and 5.25 pools are fully consumed by the 14 captains.
